transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-08-19 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (AE), Priya Patel (SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of MLOps), Markus Chen (SRE), Diego Ramos (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on request forensics, correlation tracing, and how to debug a tail-latency/error pattern.

00:00 Jordan Lee: okay everyone uh hey thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, with me is Priya the SE. uh quick intros?
00:17 Lena Ortiz: hi i'm lena, head of ml ops at CascadePharm, we run inference for clinical summarization and a few agent flows, we're seeing sporadic errors at peak and some weird latency spikes, thanks for doing this.
00:34 Priya Patel: hey lena, hi markus and diego, i'll be the one clicking through the console today. quick call plan, we'll show Trace Map, Request Inspector, logs, and then the error analysis playbook — we'll also point out what you'd need for VPC/KMS set up.
00:56 Markus Chen: sounds good, our big constraints: we need PII never to leave our VPC, we also want SSO and RBAC for teams, and we need to understand the cost delta between hosted and dedicated.
01:12 Jordan Lee: totally, we'll cover both dedicated and private patterns and call out where the console surfaces that. also note we did a SOC2 pack in the last quarter, i'll share that after this meeting.
01:29 Diego Ramos: quick question — do you keep full request bodies in logs or is it redacted by default?
01:36 Priya Patel: good callout. by default the console stores request metadata and partial payloads depending on retention policy; for Private deployments you can configure retention to zero and integrate with your KMS/HSM for encryption at rest. we also support a redaction pipeline for PII fields - it's configurable.
02:05 Priya Patel: okay i'm switching to the demo tenant — starting at the Trace Map, you can see requests grouped by correlation id, latency heatmap, and a histogram of tail latencies. note the map is sampled but we let you increase sampling for short benchmark windows.
02:30 [screen click noises]
02:45 Priya Patel: here's an example spike — you can hover to see the request_id and then jump to Request Inspector which stitches logs, model variant, and any fallback events.
03:10 Lena Ortiz: the request ids in our system look like: svc-api-20270819-<hex>. can you ingest our format so we can correlate across our logs?
03:22 Priya Patel: yes, you can provide a regex for the correlation id in the Console settings or include a header. we'll show how to map that in the playroom.
03:45 Jordan Lee: one thing we often see is a high KV cache miss rate causing extra decode time — priya will show the cache waterfall.
04:02 Priya Patel: jumping to the KV cache view — okay this visual shows hot prefixes, cache hit/miss ratio over time and per-model. you can group by model_variant and sequence_length which matters a lot for decode time.
04:28 Markus Chen: is that the same as prefix caching? sometimes our prompts have a long shared prefix for patients and that should be reused.
04:35 Priya Patel: exactly, prefix cache is captured here. if you see misses it's usually either model variant mismatch or a tokenization difference; we have a tokenizer normalization checkbox, but for Private deployments you might want to pin a quantized variant.
05:02 Lena Ortiz: okay and when a request falls back to a smaller model, does the trace show that event?
05:09 Priya Patel: yes — fallbacks and automatic model variants are annotated in the trace, you'll see an event like "fallback: variant-x -> variant-y due to queued tokens" with timestamps.
05:27 [brief crosstalk]
05:40 Priya Patel: switching to Request Inspector — each row shows request_id, correlation_id, model_variant, tokens_in/out, latency breakdown (queue, decode, kernel, network), and linked logs.
06:01 Priya Patel: i'll click into a failing request now — you can see the stack: client->gateway latency small, queued time spiked, decode kernel time high. below we show the raw logs with a fuzzy transcription overlay and any function call outputs.
06:30 Markus Chen: sometimes our logs use different timezones, does the Console normalize times?
06:36 Priya Patel: yes, everything's rendered in your org timezone but raw logs keep original timestamps, we also show a unified timeline in UTC for cross-region debugging.
06:50 Lena Ortiz: what about structured output assertions — our QA has custom checks that determine quality regressions. can we attach an alerts set to specific request_ids?
07:05 Jordan Lee: yep, Redwood Optimize can run eval sets and tie regressions to prompt sets; in the Console you can pin test prompts and then get alerted when model output quality deviates. we'll include that in the pilot scope.
07:30 Priya Patel: demoing the error analysis playbook — first step we recommend: reproduce the request using the replay feature, change model variants, and toggle prefix cache and batching. this helps isolate whether it's an algorithmic issue vs infra.
07:58 [screen click]
08:15 Priya Patel: here's a replay of a cached request — note how the timeline collapses because prefix cache takes effect. when we disable the cache the decode time jumps and we can see the exact token where the mismatch happens.
08:42 Diego Ramos: does replay rehydrate KV cache?
08:46 Priya Patel: by default replay simulates same conditions and can optionally force cold cache so you can see warm vs cold behavior. for benchmarks you can run both.
09:05 Markus Chen: we've been seeing intermittent "model oom" errors during spikes — is that captured?
09:12 Priya Patel: yes you will see OOM events annotated; there's also an infra trace which shows GPU memory pressure and whether the request timed out or retried. we also surface whether an autoscaler event was triggered.
09:30 Jordan Lee: for dedicated capacity customers we offer reserve pools and burst lanes — that often removes OOMs in sustained windows.
09:40 Lena Ortiz: curious about cost tradeoff — if we pin dedicated capacity at a high level to avoid OOMs, what's the expected unit cost change?
09:52 Jordan Lee: it's workload dependent but we can model it — cost per token can drop with batching and prefix caching, but reserved capacity has fixed commit costs. we'll run a cost model during the pilot.
10:12 Priya Patel: switching to Logs — the Console links request to your logs (we can attach your CloudWatch/Stackdriver/ELK pointers) so you get one-click jump. here you can filter by correlation_id and show only ERROR-level lines.
10:36 [screen click]
10:50 Priya Patel: sometimes transcription isn't perfect — the auto-transcript will have gibberish for proper names; but log lines are verbatim from your sources.
11:06 Markus Chen: SSO and audit logs — we need per-user action audit for compliance.
11:12 Priya Patel: audit logs are exported to your S3 or to a SIEM via syslog; we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and role-based RBAC.
11:30 Jordan Lee: ok we're at ~11 minutes in — anything urgent we should cover?
11:36 Lena Ortiz: timeline: we'd like to pilot in Q3, ideally end of August to early September. success criteria: < 99th percentile latency improvement or stable latency under production load and no PII egress.
11:57 Jordan Lee: noted, we'll target that.
12:10 Priya Patel: showing the fallback policy UI: you can set fallback rules by latency, error rate, or queue depth. policy can be canary -> full rollout and we annotate rollouts in traces.
12:34 Markus Chen: do you offer canary against a quantized variant? we worry about hallucination/regression when jumping precision.
12:42 Priya Patel: yes, and Redwood Optimize can run AB quality checks on the canary outputs; you can block rollout if eval metrics degrade.
12:58 [pause]
13:10 Priya Patel: quick note on privacy — for Private deployments your control plane can be put in your VPC; telemetry can be forwarded only as metadata and never send full prompts. we'll attach the network diagram after.
13:34 Diego Ramos: how does KMS integration work for keys, do you rotate?
13:38 Jordan Lee: we support cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) and HSM — keys can be rotated and we keep a ledger for key operations for audits.
13:54 Priya Patel: jumping to the request correlation timeline — notice how you can align application logs, model trace events, and infra traces, then mark a hypothesis. you can export a zipped packet for an SRE postmortem.
14:20 Lena Ortiz: can analysts add notes to traces? we want our triage runbook to live next to the trace.
14:26 Priya Patel: yes notes and tags are supported; you can also create a "runbook step" directly from a trace and assign an action to someone.
14:45 Markus Chen: what about retention and cost — logs plus traces could grow. how do we manage retention economically?
14:52 Jordan Lee: you can set retention buckets per environment; for long term you can offload raw traces to S3 at lower fidelity and keep high-fidelity traces for X days. our console gives cost estimates per retention policy.
15:18 Priya Patel: now a short deep-dive: kernel level timing — sometimes folks call kernel time "decode" but on some GPUs it's actually kernel+memcpy. we try to surface both.
15:38 [brief laughter]
15:45 Priya Patel: here's an example where network jitter in a cross-region call added 30ms; the trace shows network spikes before the decode starts.
16:02 Lena Ortiz: our architecture is multi-region, double proxied, so we need the trace to attribute the right hop — will Redwood accept our hop headers?
16:10 Priya Patel: yes any hop header can be used to stitch, or you can inject a custom correlation header. we'll note that for the pilot.
16:35 Jordan Lee: moving to the playbook checklist — first reproduce with replay, second check cache miss, third check model variant and quantization, fourth check infra (OOMs, gpus), fifth run a canary with Optimize.
16:52 Markus Chen: how long does it take to onboard to Private?
17:00 Jordan Lee: for Private with a standard package it's typically 6-8 weeks — that includes VPC peering, KMS, and SCIM/SSO flow. Dedicated is quicker if you can accept Redwood-managed control plane.
17:18 Diego Ramos: can we do an initial hosted pilot while we set up VPC?
17:23 Jordan Lee: absolutely — many customers start hosted with strict retention configs and then move to Private once they're happy.
17:35 Priya Patel: quick walkthrough of the benchmark spreadsheet — we'll need sample traffic traces, a target SLO, and a window to run ramp tests. we've got a template, i'll push a copy. link: https://redwood.example.com/playbooks/cascadepharm-benchmark (demo link).
18:02 Lena Ortiz: perfect, we'll prepare scrubbed traffic for the benchmark.
18:10 Priya Patel: another quick feature — Request Forensics has an "explain" toggle that runs a short eval to surface why a token was generated, useful for hallucination triage. it's not perfect but helps narrow hypotheses.
18:35 Markus Chen: do you log recovered context when you stitch requests across calls?
18:40 Priya Patel: yes the trace stitcher will show n-previous request references for multi-turn flows.
19:00 [screen pause]
19:12 Jordan Lee: okay jumping toward Q&A 
19:18 Diego Ramos: question — in a replay for a failing request, if we change model_variant and it still fails, how do you recommend isolating the problem?
19:30 Priya Patel: isolate via disabling prefix cache, run cold cache, and then change batch size and sequence length. if the error persists, look at tokenization diffs and model outputs in the eval harness.
19:55 Lena Ortiz: do you support token-level diffs? we want to know the exact token where generation deviates.
20:02 Priya Patel: yes token diffs are in the replay view, with color-coded mismatches.
20:20 Markus Chen: what telemetry do you need from our side to make investigations quick?
20:25 Priya Patel: sample request payloads, correlation id mapping, recent spike windows (logs), and a baseline SLO. that plus an IAM user with read-only access for the pilot.
20:40 Jordan Lee: we'll provide a checklist after.
20:46 Lena Ortiz: anything else on compliance? we need data residency in EU for certain clinical flows.
20:53 Jordan Lee: we have EU regions and also Private deployments that keep everything on-prem. we'll call out which artifacts remain in region.
21:18 Priya Patel: last product note — Console integrates with Redwood Optimize recommendations; for example it will suggest increasing prefix cache size or changing batching size and simulate estimated cost savings.
21:38 Markus Chen: can Optimize recommend quantization levels per model?
21:42 Priya Patel: yes it suggests quantization and estimates quality delta based on your eval prompts.
21:55 Jordan Lee: quick recap: send SOC2 and security docs, Priya to provision demo token + push benchmark template, Markus to share sample logs and correlation id format, schedule pilot window.
22:12 Lena Ortiz: thanks, that's helpful.
22:18 Diego Ramos: one more small ask — can you produce a short runbook PDF we can hand to our oncall team?
22:25 Jordan Lee: yes we'll attach a runbook and playbook — short doc.
22:33 [closing notes]
22:40 Jordan Lee: okay we'll follow up with artifacts and I'll email the recording. thanks everyone.
22:48 Lena Ortiz: thanks all.
22:52 [call ends]

Notes: transcription contains some imperfectly transcribed product names and a few timestamps may be off. Screen clicks and pauses are noted where relevant. Links shared during call: demo playbook (redwood playbook link), security doc (to be sent), benchmark template (to be pushed).
questions: Do you support KMS/HSM integration for Private?
How are fallbacks annotated in traces?
